top_story: Trump’s 7 April threat that “a whole civilisation” could die if Iran resisted US demands sharpened pressure around the Strait of Hormuz, but within hours Washington shifted from coercive escalation to a 14-day bombing pause and, by 8 April, to a provisional ceasefire with Tehran. Pakistan’s intervention appears to have helped turn an imminent maritime and regional energy crisis into a fragile de-escalation, reinforced by Tehran’s pledge to reopen the strait and Washington’s retreat from maximalist surrender terms. Gaza sits outside that easing cycle: Israeli strikes on a school killed 10 people as siege conditions deepened a catastrophic health emergency, underscoring that regional diplomacy is reducing interstate risk faster than it is alleviating civilian suffering.
